research_scope: Five full reviews of random-variable independence, pairwise independence, outer measure and adapted processes; retain previously classified power-set occurrence; no source additions or aliases.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed complete probability and stochastic process source formulations and all previously classified references; differentiated independence axioms, outer-measure axioms and continuous-time filtration structures.
amendments.reason: Source-free contextual review, preserving the already-classified power-set prerequisite; global mathematical consistency audit remains mandatory.

references.context: Probability theory: σ(X_n)={X_n^{-1}(B):B∈Σ_S}, σ-algebra of all preimages of measurable codomain sets under random variable X_n.
references.reason: This generated σ-algebra is reusable separately from mutual independence.

references.context: Measure theory: measurable space (S,Σ_S), a set with σ-algebra, shared as codomain of the sequence of random variables.
references.reason: The target measurable-space structure is independently useful.
references.matching_note: Do not assume the random variables are real-valued.

references.disposition: Definition makes sigma-algebra independence primary, rather than pairwise independence of random variables.

references.phrase: pair of independent sigma algebras special case
finite selection of pairwise distinct indices
references.disposition: Selecting all finite tuples of distinct indices is part of the mutual independence quantification.
Factorization of joint probabilities for each finite selection is the defining mutual-independence predicate, not an independently assumed notion.

references.phrase: mutual independence is stronger than pairwise
references.disposition: Factorization required for arbitrary finite index selections, not only m=2.

references.context: Probability theory: indexed family (A_i)_{i∈I} of measurable events A_i∈𝔽 in a common probability space.
references.reason: An indexed measurable-event family is independent prerequisite data.
references.matching_note: Distinguish from an indexed collection of random variables.

references.disposition: The condition i≠j specifies the defining pairwise quantification, which does not imply joint mutual independence.
Higher-order joint independence is not guaranteed by the pairwise product conditions.

references.phrase: mapping from P(X) into extended nonnegative reals
nonnegative integers or positive countable sequence indices

references.context: Set theory: power set of an arbitrary underlying set X, namely the collection of all subsets of X; variable names X and S are interchangeable.
references.matching_note: Consolidated original notation 'power set P(X)' into the same set-theoretic power-set concept; no suitably typed meaning occurs among existing meanings.

references.context: Extended nonnegative real numbers [0,+∞], including every finite nonnegative real and an element +∞, with extended sums.
references.reason: The codomain of an outer measure is an independent extended-number structure.
references.matching_note: Ordinary nonnegative real numbers alone are insufficient.

references.disposition: Outer measure of the empty set being zero is its defining normalization axiom.

references.phrase: monotonicity A subseteq B implies mu*(A)<=mu*(B)
references.disposition: Monotonicity with respect to inclusion is a defining axiom of outer measure, not separate pre-existing outer-measure data.
Countable subadditivity is the defining outer-measure axiom, not exact additivity for disjoint measurable events.
No measurable-set domain restriction or countable exact-additivity claim imposed.

references.context: Stochastic process theory: increasing σ-algebra family (𝔽_t) indexed by all t∈[0,+∞) with 𝔽_s⊆𝔽_t whenever s≤t.
references.reason: A continuous-time filtration differs from one indexed by discrete integers.
references.matching_note: Scope audit: an existing separate reference targets discrete-filtration meaning, which may be overly restrictive here.

references.disposition: Measurability of each X_t against 𝔽_t is precisely the defining adaptedness requirement; ordinary random-variable measurability is already linked.
Continuous indexing t does not mean sample paths t↦X_t are continuous.
